title: Share or keep?

slides.title: Public or private?
slides.text: Public gets you seen and found. Private keeps you safe. A good choice names the tradeoff.
slides.alt: Would you rather: share one photo with the whole world, or share ten photos with ten friends?

focus.cue: Public: seen and found by everyone
Private: safe with people you know

slides.title: Tricks start with public facts
slides.text: Most tricks start with facts that are already public: a name, a school, a daily route. Fooling people into giving away more is social engineering.
slides.alt: A card that says it is from Your bank, but carries an unknown sender badge: the name is faked.

focus.cue: A trick borrows a name you trust

slides.title: Post your art?
slides.text: Weigh both sides before you make something public.
steps: risk: a school logo in the photo shows where you are
slides.alt: Would you rather: everyone online can see your drawing, or only your family can see it?

focus.cue: Public: people enjoy it, you get feedback
Private: no one learns where you are

slides.title: Build on others' work
slides.text: Real programs reuse other people's code, art and sound. The license says what you may do. Attribution is credit written the way the license asks.
slides.alt: Three My Blocks carry plain-language notes: Sweep picks up the gems, Drop drives down the side, Home drives to the goal.

focus.cue: Reused blocks carry notes: what each one does
Credit what you reuse, the way its license asks

slides.title: Your footprint
slides.text: Everything you post adds to your digital footprint. Before you post, ask: what could someone do with this?
slides.alt: Share or Shield: where you live. Good side: friends could send you a card. Risk: a stranger could turn up at your door.

focus.cue: Before you post: what could someone do with it?

words.means: tricking people into giving away information
faking who a message is from
everything about you that can be found online
credit given the way the license asks

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Write the credit line for a game that reuses a template, some art and a free sound. Then name one thing you keep private online and the tradeoff of keeping it private.
slides.alt: Would you rather: use a picture someone else made and credit them, or draw your own, even if it is worse?

focus.cue: Reuse art: write the credit line

talk: Why share anything at all? What is worth the risk?
